title: Variance and maximum product influence
statement: Let $\Omega$ be a finite nonempty set, let $\pi$ be a probability mass function that assigns positive probability to every element of $\Omega$, and let $\iota$ be a finite nonempty index set. Suppose the real vector space of functions on $\Omega$ has a basis indexed by $\iota$ whose distinguished vector is the constant-one function and which is orthonormal for the $\pi$-weighted inner product. For any $n\ge 0$ and any function $f:\Omega^n\to\mathbb R$ taking only the values $-1$ and $1$ and not constant, the variance of $f$ under the product distribution $\pi^n$, divided by the infimum of the average query costs of randomized decision trees computing $f$ with zero error, is at most the maximum coordinate influence of $f$.
hypotheses_covered: $\pi$ is a probability mass function with full support
$\iota$ is finite and nonempty and has decidable equality
There is a real basis of functions on $\Omega$ indexed by $\iota$
The distinguished basis vector is constant one
The basis is orthonormal for the $\pi$-weighted inner product
